standard.title: Significant Australian events, symbols and identity
standard.description: significant events, symbols and emblems that are important to Australia's identity and diversity, and how they are celebrated, commemorated or recognised in Australia, including Australia Day, Anzac Day, NAIDOC Week, National Sorry Day, Easter, Christmas, and other religious and cultural festivals
standard.prior_knowledge: From Foundation (AC9HSFK02) and Y2 (AC9HS2K01): Students explored celebrations, commemorations and local significance. They understand social, cultural and spiritual significance.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students identify and explain significant Australian events, symbols and emblems and describe how they are celebrated, commemorated or recognised, including multiple perspectives on their significance.

nodes.label: National celebrations and commemorations
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify significant Australian celebrations and commemorations (Australia Day, Anzac Day, NAIDOC Week, National Sorry Day, Easter, Christmas, Lunar New Year, Diwali, Eid) and describe their historical origins.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least three significant Australian celebrations or commemorations and describe the historical origin of at least one.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and discuss historical origins of important Australian celebrations and commemorations; recognise multiple perspectives on some events (e.g. 'Invasion Day' perspectives on Australia Day); explore local, state/territory, national and religious events.
wider: Compare how Australia Day is viewed by different community groups and discuss why the date is contested
Investigate the origins of NAIDOC Week and National Sorry Day and explain their significance to First Nations Australians
nodes.hinge_reason: Students need factual knowledge of what events and symbols exist before they can discuss their significance or the perspectives different groups hold.

response_modes.reason: Build a class calendar of events with associated origins before moving to significance analysis.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The contested nature of Australia Day and the range of cultural festivals in the class creates a genuinely rich context for exploring multiple perspectives on national identity.
success_criteria: Identifies at least three significant Australian celebrations or commemorations
Describes the historical origin of at least one

nodes.label: Symbols and emblems
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify a range of Australian symbols and emblems, describe their origins and use, and explain what they represent about Australia's identity.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least three symbols or emblems and describe what each represents.
nodes.typical_width: Generate a list of local, state/territory, national and religious symbols and emblems; discuss their origins, use and significance; examine symbolism in flag design and positioning; identify when flags are flown.
wider: Examine the symbolism in the design of the Australian flag and First Nations Australian flags, comparing what each represents
Investigate the protocols around flag flying and the roles, rights and responsibilities of community members

response_modes.reason: Symbols from different cultural and religious traditions in the class community give genuine breadth to the concept of identity symbols.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The class's cultural diversity means symbols from multiple traditions will be represented — authentic comparison is available.
success_criteria: Identifies at least three symbols or emblems from different contexts
Explains what at least one symbol represents about identity
